utterances.text: Aside from the one time you've already told us where you reported Popovic's communications to you, did you ever keep your commander Blagojevic informed of the process of reburial?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. Commander Blagojevic was aware of my involvement and the involvement of the other officers and members of the military police platoon, and I regularly informed him about the situation and the progress of the reburial of those corpses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us just the rough locations where some of the bodies were reburied to.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say approximately, and only approximately because Dragisa Jovanovic selected the locations for those graves for the reburial of bodies. I know it was along the road in the region, that is, the road Zeleni Jadar towards Zenovo. And certain gravesites were in different places. One or two -- I knew of one, the exact location was near the village of Zaluzje. The next one was in the Muslim cemetery in the Budak cemetery. Another mass grave in the village of Becevo. And I knew more or less where all the graves were in which the Muslims were reburied. I want to say here that I personally was present at two gravesites. The first one is the one towards the village of Zaluzje, along that road. And I was at another gravesite. And that is the one in the village of Becevo. The one gravesite that I was at near Zaluzje was dug by Bibi Sretan who manned the excavator, and the other one was dug by Canuga. I don't know his surname.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, is it possible for you to provide a map to the witness so that we could know the exact location of these gravesites.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, some of those he knows about; others, as he has said, he doesn't really know the exact locations. We have identified all those sites, and we have that for Your Honours. I can bring in a map and ask him to point at it so you can get a feel for the areas. That's not difficult. In fact, I can do that right now. If we can put this on the ELMO. And this is Prosecutor's P85. It's a map, it's not a military map. But it is an exhibit-type map of the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there should be a pointer, Mr. Nikolic. So if you could first point to the area of Zelani Jadar which is I believe where you said some graves. Just look at the map as it's sitting on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can barely see the inscriptions. The image is not clear. Could you move it up, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Keep going, keep going. Sorry, we now have a -- in front of the screen. Right there it pretty good. Mr. Nikolic, if I can look at the map itself, don't worry about the screen in front of you. Look at the map to your right.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is Zelani Jadar here. And a number of the gravesites are along this route here towards Srebrenica. This is Srebrenica. So it's on the road towards Zelani Jadar. I think two are in the village of Ljubisavici. And the next gravesites are on the road from Zelani Jadar towards Jasenovi. I don't see it here, Jasenovi, towards Milici actually, going from Zelani Jadar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Milici by that map -- so Milici by this map would be in a westerly direction?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you point out Glogova for us, where the bodies originated?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Glogova would be on the road between Bratunac and Kravica. If I may just look at it more closely. Here is Bratunac. And going from Bratunac at the six kilometre towards the village -- no, the fourth or fifth kilometre along this road from Bratunac to Kravica in the village of Glogova was this large mass grave from which the bodies were reburied to the places I have referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honour, this map is roughly to scale. Each square represents a kilometre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Nikolic, one other question on that topic. You told us you received information about 80 to a hundred bodies from the school area in Bratunac from, I think, Dragan Mirkovic. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any information from him where those bodies were deposited?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Dragan Mirkovic also informed me that the killed Muslims killed in the night between the 13th and the 14th had been collected during the night and in the early morning of the 14th and transferred into the surroundings of Glogova in an isolated place close to Avdagina Njiva, and that they were just covered by earth and buried in that way. Unloaded and covered by earth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "unloaded," did you receive information of how they were unloaded or how they were deposited?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Dragan Mirkovic told me that representatives of the civilian authorities had asked for a truck from his company which was a FAP 13, a truck that can lift -- the back of which can be lifted, and in that way the load deposited.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you provided information about the geographic description of the area that they were unloaded in?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He told me then that this was done in an area which is about 1 kilometre away from this mass grave and that when you come to Avdagina Njiva village, you take a return to the right. And after a certain distance, this was done where there is no settlement. In the broader area of Avdagina Njiva. He mentioned the village of Halilovici. I don't know where that village is situated, but I do know the road and where it leads to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any point after the fall of the Srebrenica enclave did you receive instructions to destroy documents?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the fall of Srebrenica, I did not receive instructions to destroy documents. But I can explain what I did with the documents when handing over my treasury box when I was delivering the documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us what, if anything, you did related to Srebrenica-type documents.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the handing over of the safe, I was no longer chief of the security and intelligence organ in the brigade. All the documents which had anything to do with Srebrenica I destroyed, set light to them, in the presence of a commission from the corps command and in the presence of the officer to whom I handed over the safe and whatever was in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by "commission"? What is this commission from the corps command you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a group of three officers who came to Bratunac for a record to be made in its presence and for the safe and documents to be handed over in their presence. The safe and everything inside so that a commission should be present and a report compiled, and this handed over to the officer designated to be my successor in the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where did the -- why did you destroy documents?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I destroyed them -- I destroyed everything that I thought at that point in time could compromise me and the brigade, so I destroyed it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you received any instructions from anyone to do that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't receive instructions from anyone to do that. I did it myself because I felt that my documents, those that were not conveyed to the archives, should not be passed on to my successor who simply had not worked in that body before coming to replace me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of documents did you destroy?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I destroyed all the documents relating to the period, that is, reports around Srebrenica, before the beginning of operations, during the operations, following the operations about which I reported to the command of the Drina Corps. Therefore, all written documents and reports that I had in my safe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about what date did this occur, the destruction of the documents?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot tell you when that was. I can just say approximately that I destroyed those documents after I left the Bratunac Brigade. I went to take up duties as head of department in the ministry for displaced persons after which the request came for me to go to the command and destroy those documents. So after I left the command of the Bratunac Brigade. I was no longer performing those duties, but I hadn't in the meantime handed over the keys of the safe, nor the documents. So I'm not able to tell you the exact date when this was done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that you destroyed the documents on your own, and you've just said that there was a request from the brigade command to come over and destroy the documents. Can you clear that up for us. What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said that the request came from the brigade command for me to hand over the safe. And in that request, there was no indication anywhere that I should destroy the documents. So from the brigade command, the request arrived for me to come and hand over my safe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you destroyed the documents, was there anybody present that witnessed that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I set fire to the documents the chief of security of the Drina Corps was present, Major Pajic. Also present were two other commanding officers from the corps command who constituted the commission of the corps command for the handing over of documents, and also Captain Lazar Ostojic, an officer of the Bratunac Brigade, to whom I was handing over the safe and the documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of those people object to you destroying the documents in their presence?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, can you give us just a rough estimate of when this would have occurred.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really am not able to guess. I can't tell you when this was. I know that I wasn't working there any more, that I was called in. But I can't tell you when that was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remind us when you left the Bratunac Brigade or when your employment with them stopped.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can. Officially, I was demobilised on the 20th of April, 1996. But I must also add that even after being decommissioned and after I had started working in the ministry for refugees and displaced persons, for a short while, I continued to perform the duty. And for a while, I did continue reporting about events in Bratunac, especially the events linked to the involvement of UNPROFOR units and certain individuals, reporters and others who came to Bratunac. That was, I wish to remind you that this was an agreement that had been reached between me and my superior officer from the corps command, Mr. Popovic. They would allow me to move to this new ministry, but until a new officer is appointed, that I should continue working in that area should the need arise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You referred to one of the Drina Corps officers present at the destruction of the document as the chief of security. Can you tell us again who that was.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Major Pajic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to Lieutenant-Colonel Vujadin Popovic who, as you described, at the time of the events was the chief of security for the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic was chief of security of the corps when I was about to take up new duties in the ministry for refugees and displaced persons, and I was referring to that period. But in the period when I was handing over my safe, the chief of security was Major Pajic. And I think that this was perhaps a month, two, or three after I had already left the Bratunac Brigade. Maybe it wasn't that long, but certainly Vujadin Popovic had left the corps command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the first name of this Major Pajic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew it, but I really can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've already described at the time of the events that the chief of staff of the Bratunac Brigade was a -- was named Pajic. Is this the same Pajic or a different Pajic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. He has nothing to do with Novica Pajic, who was chief of staff of the Bratunac Brigade. This was an officer from the command of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have a couple of short videoclips, a few documents, and it's looking good for ending before the end of the day. And I will just start with the videoclips. We're hoping that the audiovisual will work. And I would just be asking the witness a few questions about the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, during this sitting, we just have five minutes. So you just tell me when you are ready to stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. We might be able to finish the video in that five minutes, or at least some of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, I want to show you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And Mr. President, these are videos that we've all seen already. They're just clips from the exhibits that are already in evidence. The first one we have marked as P88 so that you can see it separately. And it's from 12 July before the meeting at the Hotel Fontana. And if we could just run that video, and if we could -- I'm going to stop it if possible at a particular place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could stop it there. Your Honour, again I have got two different versions that are both -- one is not very visible. If I could walk over and see what the witness can see, I can tell whether or not I can ask him questions about it. I have a hard copy if his screen is not working very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Looks okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In looking at this still, can you first tell us where this is.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a shot taken in front of the Fontana Hotel in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know about what time this is, what day this is and what time?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the 12th of July, 1995, after the meeting held at 10.00; that is, after the meeting ended on the 12th of July, the third meeting in the Fontana Hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell us who these individuals are starting with the person on the far left of the screen.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first person on the left is me, Momir Nikolic. The next person that can be seen going from the left, the second person, is Colonel Jankovic. The person in the doorway is a person from the personal security of General Mladic. And the last person in this row is Lieutenant-Colonel Vujadin Popovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If we could let the video run.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could you stop it again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this particular still, can you tell us where that is.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is also in front of the hotel in Bratunac at the entrance to the hotel itself, the area in front of the hotel leading to the entrance to the hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell what -- at what time and day this is.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can see, I believe this was also on the 12th. I can't see what goes on after this, but I think this is the 12th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you identify any of those individuals that we see, the three people. And again, starting with the far left, the person in the background.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person standing in the background is the DutchBat commander, Colonel Karremans. Second person with his back turned towards the camera, as far as I can identify, is Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic, Vujadin Popovic. And the person wearing a moustache is Lieutenant-Colonel Kosoric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if this is before or after the meeting at the Hotel Fontana on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if we could just continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is this? Who's arriving here?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You can just let it play. Stop.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here, you can see the Muslim delegation arriving in Bratunac, in the area outside the Fontana Hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you name the people, again, from the left to the right, or whatever you can remember.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the background, there's a security man, the far left, General Mladic's security. The next person you can see is the one wearing the white shirt. That's Ibro Nuhanovic. Next to him, a lady whose name I can't remember. I know who she was. She was a member of the delegation. And the far right, you can see Nesib Mandzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think we can just finish it out. Okay. Mr. President, that may be a good time. And I'm hopeful that we'll be able to finish up in the last session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon all Your Honours. I see you're all back. I would just play another video section, and this is videoclip P89. And I'll just ask the witness if he recognises anybody in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the person that is speaking into the microphone now?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is General Krstic. As far as I know, at that time he was the chief of staff of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it's of an unfortunately bad quality, but if you recognise anyone else as this finishes up, just let us know if you could. But the quality is not great.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can see right now, I don't recognise any of the soldiers surrounding him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We'll just play this clip. It's the clip next to this that I want to get to. But this won't take long. If you do recognise anyone, let us know.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If we could freeze that.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this frozen image, I recognise Zoran Kovacevic, a member of the Bratunac Brigade. I think he was either the deputy commander or the commander of one of the companies that were part of the 2nd infantry battalion of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you have any personal contact with him while you were in Potocari on the 12th or 13th?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I was not in touch with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I could ask this still of this -- of a shot of this person that is of a better quality be put on the ELMO. It's the same basic P22, but it's page 22, chapter 10, P9 of that large exhibit which is already into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I surely don't wish to interrupt, but he's already identified. It's already into evidence. May I ask what the relevancy of now going back to the photograph as opposed to the video that we just watched, especially since the Court is concerned about time efficiency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, once the evidence is admitted into evidence, it does not mean that we will put much weight on that piece of evidence. It has to be shown to the witnesses to see whether they could recognise it or not. But of course, I agree with you, we could go through this as quickly as possible since we have already admitted it into evidence. But Mr. McCloskey, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. This is a little clearer shot, I hope, of that similar frame.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've already identified the gentleman in front of it, Kovacevic. But over his left shoulder, do you see that person just over the left shoulder of Mr. Kovacevic? And I can't tell - I'm sorry - if that is on the screen or not. I don't know if we have an ELMO image yet, Your Honours. And I apologise for that. I can't seem to get it to come up on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see anything on my screen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, just take a look at that exhibit. Do you recognise someone besides Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To the right from where I'm looking from, this is a person wearing a moustache. This is Lieutenant-Colonel Kosoric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you just take a pen there and put a circle around the person you're identifying as Kosoric. And just put your initials there, if you could.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's -- if you could show that to Mr. Karnavas so he could see, and of course Defence counsel. It's not a huge issue, but this is the old-fashioned way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. If we could play this one out, this -- and go to the next videoclip.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise any of those other guys in this thing, in this image?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The frame I'm looking at right now, I can't recognise anyone else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Then let's continue. Okay. If we could play the next clip.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise anyone in this clip?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise a person nicknamed Gargija. I'll probably remember his name. Right now, I can't remember, but I'm sure I will.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you point out where on the image on the screen that we see this.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, where I'm looking from, to the far right of the screen, the person is carrying some kind of barrel of a weapon, I think. I can't see clearly. The still is not very clear. I think he's also wearing a bandanna.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And for the record, this is P90.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's that person on the far right of the screen that you -- is nicknamed Gargija?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's the person I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where this is, this scene on this image?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can tell, this is a photo from the Potocari area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Gargija, do you know what unit he was from?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, as far as I know, he was a member of the special brigade unit, the Panthers, from Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What corps would that be?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think at the time that was the East Bosnia Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could continue that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about this person on the far right of the screen? Do you recognise this person?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This person at the far right wearing a bandanna is a person nicknamed Lika.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know his full name?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that person's full name at the moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what unit he was in at the time, in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he was a member of the Bratunac Brigade. Now, whether he was a member of the 3rd infantry battalion, I'm not sure. But I think he was probably a member of the 3rd infantry battalion. At any rate, he was certainly a member of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything else about this group of people that we saw here, including Lika and Gargija? I'm sorry, not this group; that's another group. But just the guys as they were walking in on the earlier part of this, or do you know anything about them?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all I can tell you about those two soldiers is what I thought about them, what my personal position was. I think they both belonged to the group of soldiers that I would describe as problematic. Gargija, the first man, had left the brigade pursuant to his own request. In a manner of speaking, he wanted to avoid being in the Bratunac Brigade and the Srebrenica area. That was the reason. As for the other man, the other soldier, he was a person who always created problems for the police of the Bratunac Brigade. He would leave his unit without authorisation, and they often had to take him in. My opinion is that those two soldiers were problematic and displayed an obvious lack of discipline.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us know if you're able to identify anybody in these photos.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What we can see now from the back -- the image is too fast. I can't see right now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see any more. I can only see a fraction of -- I can't identify the person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Gargija, I think, the person I've just seen. This is the same person I have already identified as Gargija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This person here, these people, this person holding a child, this is a Muslim I know personally. He used to work as a driver. Can you just rewind a little bit because I can no longer see it now. The previous.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Hold on a second. It takes a bit to rewind.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This man waving his hand -- now he's gone again. I know him personally. He is the driver who worked in the Vihor Bratunac Transport Company. Can you just rewind to the previous frame, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bear with us. This is a new technology we're trying to get used to.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This man here holding the child, that's the driver's son. I recognise him because I was his teacher at the secondary school. The son of the man you're showing now is the man holding the child.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And who is the man we're showing now with his hand out towards the camera?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the man I was talking about. I can't remember his name, but I do know this man personally. He used to work before the war for the Vihor Bratunac Transport Company. He worked there as a driver. But I really don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if he survived Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know what became of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, just to clarify the record, this man did, in fact, survive Srebrenica. I don't want to leave a false impression with the Court. If we could continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. To the left on my screen, I recognise Mr. Ljubisa Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, there's a group approaching to the left. At the foreground, we can see General Mladic. To the right wearing a flak jacket is a man who was in charge of General Mladic's security. General Mladic. At the front, I believe I recognised Mr. Kingori. I met him personally during talks prior to the fall of the enclave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the UNMO officer from Africa?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I think -- actually I know that's the officer I'm talking about whom I met. Yes. I met Mr. Kingori a number of times before the enclave was attacked. At the far right, I can see a man wearing a moustache and sunglasses. This is Mr. Dusko Jevic from the police, the MUP special brigade. Yes, you can see it clearly now. Here again we see General Mladic to the left. This is when General Mladic addressed those present the first time he came to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What date was that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was -- that was on the 12th when he spoke to the civilians present, rather assembled in Potocari. General Mladic and the people from his personal security.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is segment number P93.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see a group of soldiers on the screen on the road between the Zuti Most checkpoint and Potocari. To the left -- the far left of the image, at least on my screen, I can see a soldier whose last name is Stevic. Next to him is a soldier whose last name is Radic. The next soldier standing down the middle of the screen with a rifle slung across his shoulder is soldier Vuksic. All three of these soldiers as far as I know belonged to the 2nd infantry battalion of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I want to finish playing this little segment of these soldiers, and just watch what they are doing because I want to ask you a question about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those soldiers that you described, can you tell us what they were doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: A foundation needs to be laid first of all. He watched a video, and they seemed to be sitting there. We can all draw a conclusion as to what they might be doing. If we can lay a foundation as to whether he saw those gentlemen over there on that particular day, whether he tasked them, or he knows they were tasked, I don't have a problem. But as of right now no foundation has been made for this gentleman to give a speculative answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey, you have to ask whether this witness was there during that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I can, Your Honour. We have been through this already. But I can ask him again if you'd like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what day these soldiers are standing there in this position?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where they were standing just now, I know that that was on the 12th of July in the afternoon, in the early afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what units they belonged to?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The soldiers I just saw belonged to the 2nd infantry battalion of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall being present at this scene where these soldiers are standing, or you could see these guys standing there like that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could see them, but I wasn't present there. At the time I was in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. Were you present to be able to see these guys standing there at the time, or...? I think we have a little confusion here. Do you remember this scene that is depicted in the video?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that I do remember those soldiers. But I wasn't there with them just then, but I remember those soldiers who were on that segment of the road towards Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And can you tell by looking at this video which -- what these particular soldiers are doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Same objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Same objection. A foundation has not been able to be established, so I have the same foundation. He's asking the witness now to speculate. The Court has seen the video, the Court can draw its own conclusions. If Mr. McCloskey has other witnesses that he can bring other witnesses that he can bring forward such as this particular gentleman that are shown in the footage, that's fine, but through this, I'm afraid as far as I'm concerned he is unable to make any determination as to what these gentlemen were doing. And it seems to me they were just standing there, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, since there is no sound foundation, I hope you could drop this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, yesterday this witness testified that he was the one in charge of organising and facilitating the actions of various units in Potocari. He named the infantry battalions that these folks are from and said that they were present doing perimeter security, is my best recollection. And with that in mind, and having him see this video, I just want to ask him, you know, what are they doing, if he knows. Is this the perimeter security that he's talking about, or are these guys just standing there on a lunch break from somewhere else? He's in a perfect position to know; he's in charge of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We are talking about these particular clips of the video, and the witness has already told us he was not there when this video was shot. So it's very difficult for this witness to tell us what those people in that video are doing at that time. He may tell us what he saw and what he heard personally at that time, which may not be in this video. Now here, we are talking about this particular situation of that videoclip.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, setting aside this videoclip, you testified that you'd seen these folks in Potocari on the 12th. When you saw them, what were they doing?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, I testified and said that I saw elements of units of the 2nd infantry battalion and elements of the 3rd infantry battalion in Potocari. And in answer to your question, I can say that I do know that those men, those soldiers who were in Potocari, were assisting or working in and around the transport of civilians from Potocari in the period during which I was in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could go on to the next clip.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Here, on this still, I recognise on the right of the screen two members of the military police of the Bratunac Brigade. The first one with the rifle in his hand is policeman Radenko Zaric. And the other policeman, and you can just see his head, is a policeman from the Bratunac Brigade. His name is Milovan Mitrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This clip is Exhibit P93, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have you had a chance to see this video prior to today?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have had a chance to see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. If we could just play this, finish this out slowly so you can get an idea of how much of the faces we can see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the clip it just finished up with, were you able to get a good look at both these officers?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was able to see them well before and now. So I know that they were two officers -- military policemen, not officers, from the military police platoon of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. That's the end of the videos for now. And if I could get some assistance from the usher, I'd like to show you if you could put this on the ELMO, it's marked P86. It's an aerial image of Bratunac that the witness has had a chance to previously mark. Counsel has been provided with a copy of that. The Court should have copies also. If you could put that on the ELMO, especially the parts where you can see handwriting on it. I guess we're not having much luck with the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've already written on this document. Can you explain to us what writing you've done on this document? I think everyone should have it in front of them. Just sort of describe the writing and what you've highlighted.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I marked on this photograph the offices of the Bratunac Brigade, that is, the building of Kaolin. And I marked with an arrow where those offices were. I also marked with a circle the building in which the military police of the Bratunac Brigade, the platoon, was housed. Also, I marked with a circle the apartment block where Colonel Vidoje Blagojevic's apartment was. And also, I encircled the Fontana Hotel, marking with an arrow which building it is on this shot. And I also put my signature and the date when I marked it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If we could look at the next exhibit, P87, which is another aerial image that you've already marked which everyone should have. Can you again describe what that is that you've marked.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On this image, I have also marked and written down the names of the buildings and indicated with arrows which the buildings are. Number 1 is the Vuk Karadzic elementary school, the building that I identified. Then next to it is the gym which belonged to that same Vuk Karadzic school. Then the building known as the hangar. And at the end, the building that I identified as the secondary school centre, the old secondary school, Djuro Pucar Stari. And again, the date and my signature has been affixed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The next document that I have now, we will be very nice to have the ELMO for this, Your Honour, and perhaps we should take some kind of a break. I hate to ask that, but these are now military documents that -- or we could just standby, too, and hope...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe we could break for 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. --- Break taken at 1.14 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I hope that ELMO is okay. And we might sit a little bit longer to make up the time we lost. Mr. McCloskey, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have a few documents to ask the witness about. And most of these documents I will not be tendering through this witness because they will involve providing additional authentication and foundation through witnesses that, as you're aware and counsel is aware, to be scheduled in the future. But given the unique situation that we have an accused testifying, I will tie this up later and not offer them into evidence until they have been fully tied up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course. And after we hear the cross-examination, we will ask you to inform us what kind of documents you are going to tender through this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. The first document I want to show this witness is a record of an intercept communication intercepted by the Bosnian Muslim army. Excuse me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: By the Bosnian Muslim security services.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to voice an objection to this line of questioning at this point. In the common-law system, which Peter McCloskey and Mr. Karnavas are familiar with, and I recognise how familiar you are with it, we have something called taking the witness on voir dire, which means that the opposing counsel gets to question him about his expertise and his participation and whether he is qualified to answer this line of questioning. I would ask the Court to allow me to ask a few questions of Mr. Nikolic just to lay the foundation to see if he's qualified to answer these. It's our belief that he did not participate in any of these intercepts. He's not a communications expert, and we don't believe he has the expertise to offer the opinion of whether he believes that these intercepts are genuine or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Sinatra, I have to tell you that we are not adopting strictly the common-law system. In my legal system, all the documents is admissible at least during the proceedings, then the Judge will make his findings, our decisions, how much weight he is going to put on these documents. Secondly, we do not even know what kind of documents that Mr. McCloskey will put to this witness. Let us go along this line. And if you have opportunities, of course, you are free to raise it after the question is asked or after the answer is given. Is that fair enough?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We were provided the documents ahead of time, that's why I know what his line of questioning is before he presents them. But as long as we will be able to challenge the qualifications of this witness at some other time, I would -- I wanted to lodge our running objection to his qualifications to answer these questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much. And the -- I believe that you have the full opportunity to do so also in the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, this intercept is from the State Security Services of the Bosnian Muslim government dated 12 July, 1995. And from the heading, it appears to be between a Krstic and a Lieutenant-Colonel Krsmanovic. And Mr. Nikolic, based on just a quick reading of the substance of this, and I don't want you to read it out loud, and knowing that it's from 12 July at 0735 hours, can you tell me who you believe Lieutenant-Colonel Krsmanovic is, just briefly. And as we know, some of these people you may have talked about before.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I do object to Mr. McCloskey testifying from the document. He's reading from the document. He hasn't had the witness identify the names that are present on it. He's asking him who these people are, and the person hasn't identified -- the witness has not identified these people, so Mr. McCloskey is in reality testifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think Mr. McCloskey is just asking a very simple question to this witness. And to save time, and since this document is not going to be tendered by this witness, I believe that kind of procedure is allowed. And by that way, to my understanding that Mr. Stojanovic will deal with this witness. If the Defence counsel for Mr. Jokic have some objections, would you please be kind enough to cover your idea to the counsel who is particularly dealing with this witness and to raise it to the attention to the Court. You may proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who do you think Lieutenant-Colonel Krsmanovic is in this conversation?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Lieutenant-Colonel Krsmanovic who is mentioned in this conversations the lieutenant-colonel from the command of the Drina Corps, and that he was -- and that there was a chief of the transportation service from the command of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how about the person identified as Krstic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, on the basis of what I see here and what is written here, I think that this is General Krstic from the command of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what in particular do you think they're talking about?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of this text that I have read now, they are talking about buses which need to be provided from these mentioned municipalities and the places mentioned where those buses should come to. And the specific number is mentioned of 50 buses. And their destination, their final destination being the stadium in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any Bratunac Brigade officers that were working with Krsmanovic in -- related to buses or vehicles coming in to Bratunac on 12 July?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From the Bratunac Brigade in connection with the arrival of these buses, and other matters linked to the buses, as far as I know or what I know for certain is that the assistant commander of the Bratunac Brigade for logistics was involved, that is Major Dragoslav Trisic. And I also know that Loncarevic, Pavle, and Mr. Stevic, I don't know his first name, were also involved. These are the things that I can remember. But mainly, Dragoslav Trisic and Pavle Loncarevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were these buses used for on 12 July?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These buses were used on the 12th of July to transport the civilians and the population in general from Potocari to Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they used to transport Muslim men in the Potocari crowd to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, the same buses were used for those purposes as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If I could ask the usher, we can go to the next exhibit. She may need to stay there because I can see that the screen unfortunately doesn't fit the page, and she may need to act as the person to direct this operation. This is 65 ter number 925. And for the record, it's from the collection from 13 July, 1995, at 0705 hours. This is a Bosnian Muslim army intercept.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Nikolic, if I could ask you to just take a look at it. I know you've seen this before. And I'm just going to go down this intercept, so if we could just follow it a little bit and I'll ask you some questions. It starts out with: "Give me Nikolic." And goes on, someone says: "Nikolic hasn't arrived yet." Who do you think the Nikolic is they're talking about?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can infer from this document is that the reference is to me, Momir Nikolic, chief of the intelligence and security organ of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell from this document where this call is coming in to?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. I need to look at the beginning. On the basis of what I can see from this document, the call is from the corps command, the command of the Drina Corps. So a general is calling. The link is established through the switchboard, and on the line is Jankovic and a general from the command of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you -- who do you believe this Jankovic is?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can be seen that this is Mirko Jankovic who, in those days, was commander of the military police platoon and who that night stood in for me. He acted as the operations officer on duty in the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when it says: "Here's police commander Jankovic," you believe that's Mirko Jankovic, the commander of the military police platoon of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where would Mirko Jankovic be speaking from as he's taking part in this conversation?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirko Jankovic was speaking from the operations room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of where?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the operations room at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you identify from anything in this document who he's speaking to?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just have a minute to look through this and find the right sentence. On the basis of this sentence here towards the end of this conversation: "Where is my department commander?", on the basis of this, I can identify that this is General Zivanovic because General Zivanovic's cousin was one of the commanders of the military police platoon in the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, for the record - and I will provide the booth with the official translations in the future. We may not have given them to them. But there's an important word that was interpreted as "department commander." And in fact, as you can see from the second page referred to by Mr. Nikolic, that has been translated into English as "squad commander."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what are General Zivanovic and Mirko Jankovic talking about in this conversation? And let me just -- I'll try to be helpful. Specifically on the first page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my apologies. I just thought this was a good opportunity to clarify because of our previous intervention. This is likely to happen during the testimony of our next witness. The essential issue at stake in Dragan Jokic's Defence is the truthfulness, authenticity, and quality of the intercepts. Today, we have Momir Nikolic's testimony as to the contents of this conversation, intercepted conversation. But we have not been given an answer as to whether this witness considers the conversation as authentic, whether this conversation could have taken place at all. Does he believe that any such conversation ever took place at all? And then after that, who took part in the conversation? If he considers the conversation as authentic and if he thinks this represents an actual conversation between the MUP and the BH army representatives, that's the essence of our objection. We would like to pose the following question: These intercepts, do they qualify as proof, are they really authentic? The essential point is that we still haven't listened to all of the Prosecutor's witnesses who worked as operators manning switchboards who connected these calls or listened in on these calls. Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojanovic, I think this is another question, and I believe that the Prosecution will call other witnesses to testify to that effect. But I have some problem with the question put to this witness by Mr. McCloskey. He asked "What are General Zivanovic and Jankovic talking about in this conversation?" I don't think this is the right question to put to this witness since this witness was not present at that time. We already know that he was not in when he was asked. All he could answer is from this document. So it's useless for us. We cannot be helped by his answer at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, this particular witness should be able to provide this Chamber with his opinion regarding the terms, the phrases, the numbers, the information in this document. For example, my -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, please. Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: For example, I was going to narrow the question down to, at this point, on July 12th when the General says: "How many vehicles arrived so far and how many Turks have to be transferred?" My question would be if General Zivanovic and Mirko Jankovic are talking about the transfer of Turks on the morning of 12 July, what in your opinion would they be talking about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, this question is allowed, to the specific words of "the Turks." But not on the whole contents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I thought I might save time by that question, but I realised that that wasn't going to save time. So I went for the particular one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, the question from General Zivanovic saying "how many vehicles have arrived so far and how many Turks have to be transferred," first question, in the context of this, what would "Turks" mean?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this context, it would mean that General Zivanovic was asking about the Muslims in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And then the answer: "About one third of them have probably been transferred, about as many there are have arrived now. One third have been transferred. Around 70 vehicles have left, and around..." By the morning of 13 July at this time, 0705 hours, do you know how many of the Muslim civilians in Potocari had been transferred out of Potocari at this time?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, all I can say is what I knew and what I saw. This number was higher. On the 12th, more than one half of the Muslims present in Potocari had already been transferred. And according to my estimate, this should amount to about 15.000. I think this is Mirko Jankovic's assessment, and I cannot comment on that. What I know I think is a more accurate estimate than the one we're looking at here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And on the second page in the English, the General asks: "Where's Nikolic?" And the response is: "Nikolic went home this morning at half past 3.00." Is that true? Had you gone home at half past 3.00 that morning?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That morning, I left at about 3.00, maybe half past 3.00. Thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I don't have any other questions on that particular intercept.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could go to 65 ter number 259. It's a type listing of Bosnian bus companies, letters, and then amounts in litres. And Your Honours, for foundational purposes, we will show that this, what is a handwritten document in the B/C/S which I hope you have a copy of, was obtained in a search warrant of the Bratunac Brigade several years ago. And I merely want to ask this witness:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In looking at these handwritten notes in the Bosnian, which are dated 12 -- well, question mark 12 July, 1995, at 2100 hours," in your opinion, what is this a reference to?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of what I can see in this document, this could be a reference to buses used for transferring civilians from Potocari. What this document indicates in the first column on the left-hand side of the page is where the buses come from, from which companies, the buses used for the transport of Muslims, their registration plate numbers, Zvornik, Sarajevo, Banja Luka, and so on. And in the last column, I see the number of litres used for running those buses. This is a reference to the buses used for the evacuation from Potocari on the 12th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. On the third page of the English document, there's a list of actual names. In your opinion -- there's some names and a similar sort of list. Briefly, what in your opinion are these names?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is also dated the 12th of July, 1995. The content of the document is similar to the previous one. In addition, here we have a list of names and certain makes, types of trucks, the amounts of fuel expended. And especially in relation to the previous document, on the left-hand side of the document the way I'm looking, it says Vihor, 13th of July." This might mean the following: Number 18, 19, 20, and 22, those were the drivers, the Vihor drivers. But it could also mean something else. It could mean that these buses took their fuel from the petrol station that was within the compound of the Bratunac Transport Company which owned its own petrol station within its premises.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Setting aside this document now, from your own personal knowledge, do you know where the fuel that was provided for the vehicles that transported the Muslims on these days, 12th, 13th, and 14th, what petrol stations they came from?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I've understood your question. I'm sorry. Can you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What petrol stations did the fuel for the buses come from? Or I should say where did the fuel for the buses come from?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know where the fuel came from, from which petrol station specifically. I can't say. The interpretation I'm getting is you're asking me which petrol station did the fuel come from. I don't know that. But I do know that fuel was taken at the petrol station in Bratunac, fuel for the buses. That's what I know. The buses got their fuel at the petrol station in Bratunac. They filled up there. Another thing I know about is that for a certain period of time, fuel was being taken from the petrol station owned by the Bratunac Autotransport Company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if any members of the Bratunac Brigade were involved in the distributing of fuel for the buses that transported Muslims on the 12th, 13th, or 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Major Dragoslav Trisic personally was involved in securing the fuel and in the distribution of fuel for the buses and trucks used during the transport on the 12th and the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. If we could go to the next exhibit, 65 ter number 264. And in the Bosnian language, the originals are handwritten notes, and we have a typed version for the English. If we could put the English on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, could you just again familiarise yourself with these handwritten notes. Do you know what they are?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I see in front of me are notes on the interrogation of Mr. Resid Sinanovic. The next thing in this document that I can see is a note concerning Nazif Avdic, and Munib Delic, if my reading it correct. These are notes concerning the interrogation of prisoners during this period of time at the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this Resid Sinanovic the same one that you had delivered to the military police offices that you've testified earlier about?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It's Resid Sinanovic, son of Rahman, whom I personally brought in and handed him over to Zlatan Celanovic at the military police headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who wrote those handwritten notes regarding Resid Sinanovic and the other Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can say is that I recognise the handwriting of Zlatan Celanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to Resid Sinanovic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can say is that following the interrogation of Resid Sinanovic at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters, he was visited by a number of people, his friends, in the premises of the military police following which he was transferred to the Vuk Karadzic elementary school and following those visits. After that, I have further information he was transferred along with everyone else to Zvornik. And as far as I know, based on my information, he was shot. He's no longer alive, and neither are any of the other people who were taken there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe to us where you got your information about what happened to him from the time you delivered him to the time he was shot?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was asking questions about this specific case. There was a lot of speculation surrounding the fate of Mr. Resid Sinanovic. And some people provided this information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any specific information on the fate of the other people that are mentioned here, Nazif Avdic, Munib Dedic, Aziz Husic, Harudin Begzadic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any information on these people, no additional information. Not any kind of information, in fact. When I looked at this document, it's the first I found out of their presence at the military police building in Bratunac. I knew about Sinanovic, but as for the rest of them I had no idea. And even now, I don't know what became of those individuals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If we could go to the next document, 65 ter number 235. And if you could just briefly tell us, having looked at this, this is a one-page piece of paper now. Can you tell us what that is and where it comes from.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm looking at right now is a daily report. This is a daily report from the Bratunac Brigade military police platoon dated the 13th of July, 1995. This document says who did what as far as the military police platoon members were concerned on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this document part of a larger collection, or is it an individual document as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the military police platoon, the duty officer of the military police platoon would write a report like this on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of record-keeping was this material kept in?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was kept in the files of the military police platoon in their room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a logbook, or were these in individual files as far as you recall?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was a book made like this where reports were entered every day, the military police reports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me just ask you if we could look at that first line: "The police were engaged in securing the UNHCR and the surrender of the Muslim people from Srebrenica in Zuti Most to the Serb soldiers in Bratunac." What does that reference to UNHCR mean as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, I think this is a mistaken definition of the forces of DutchBat. Police were engaged in securing the UNHCR. I don't think that's correct. I think the police were engaged in securing members of UNPROFOR, which is perfectly correct. And I know all the detail surrounding that operation. That's one thing. So instead of UNHCR, it should say "members of DutchBat." The surrender of the Muslim people from Srebrenica in Zuti Most to the Serb soldiers in Bratunac, I think this makes little sense. It is true there was a checkpoint on Zuti Most, the yellow bridge, and whether they just considered passing through the checkpoint would have implied the surrender of Muslims, in that case, this makes sense. But certainly there was no surrender of anyone to anyone else that was being carried out on Zuti Most, the yellow bridge. Not to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the other information in this document appear to make sense, again, aside from the UNHCR references?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can go item by item. "Some of the police forces secured the sick and wounded in the clinic," yes, that was true. "Night duty in Fontana and the UNHCR," that makes sense, that was also part of their duties. Securing the commander, Ratko Mladic, that, as well. Securing the UNHCR. Again, that's a mistake. We're not talking about the UNHCR. We're talking about the DutchBat people at the school. And the remaining items are regular duties, regular service at the bridge. So the rest of the document seems perfectly accurate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where General Mladic spent the night, the night of the 12/13 July?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly where he spent that night. But I can tell you two things that would have been the only two possible things. Here, where it says "securing the commander, Ratko Mladic" --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I would like to object at this point. He was asked a question, Where did General Mladic spend the night. He indicated he didn't know. Now if Mr. McCloskey wishes to pose another question to elicit some additional information, that's fine. But now we have the witness taking control over the line of questioning and determining what he's going to testify to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, we are very interested to hear what the witness is going to tell us. It may be related to the whereabouts of Mr. Mladic at that time. Witness, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. I'm positive that throughout that period of time, while General Mladic was staying in the territory of Bratunac and Srebrenica Municipalities, his security was provided by members of the military police platoon of the Bratunac Brigade. This whole time, there was only one squad that was in charge of his personal security. Furthermore, I also know that after General Mladic had left Bratunac, he took the squad along with him to provide his personal security on the way to Zepa. Therefore, if the operations duty officer of the military police wrote "security for General Ratko Mladic," all I can add is the following: It's quite possible that what they wrote down was the involvement of that particular squad that was providing his personal security throughout this period of time and after he left. That's all I can say concerning this part of the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to go back to the aerial image of Bratunac, and I apologise, this was P86, as well as circling the Bratunac Brigade headquarters and the building for the military police, did you circle the apartment block where your commander Blagojevic lived during this time?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I did encircle the apartment blocks where Commander Blagojevic lived. Actually, in one of those buildings. I can't tell you exactly which one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, we can continue. I apologise that we're not through. We have some more documents. But we should be able to plod along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, how long do you think you could use to finish those documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Maybe half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We going to continue or are we going to break. Let me consult with the Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, I was told that some people are working very hard in this case, I mean those interpreters, court reporters. Some of them had their breakfast at 7.00. Now it's 2.15. It's very late. From the humanitarian point of view, we need a break. Maybe we could come back at 4.00 and continue, to finish the last part. Because I really want to have the whole day for Mr. Karnavas to streamline his cross-examination. We believe it's worth to have the whole period of time. So we'll continue at 4.00. But I have to tell you that I have some other engagement this afternoon, so I am very sorry that I could not be here in the afternoon's hearing. And Judge Vassylenko and Judge Argibay will continue the hearing. So we'll resume -- well, we'll resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: May I just say one thing, Your Honour. It will take less than one minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I don't know if Your Honours have noticed that we have an empty chair here. But due to the fact that the Registry refused to pay for an interpreter for communications between counsel and co-counsel, I just wanted to state that the rights of Mr. Jokic under Article 20 and 21 are being seriously violated at this point. The Registry refuses to pay for an interpreter for us to speak to each other which makes it difficult when we're trying to present the best defence for Mr. Jokic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think you've raised this issue many times. Certainly I will look into this matter by consulting with the Registrar. So we'll resume at 4.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 2.20 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody. As Judge Liu is unable to continue sitting after the break for the reasons of the Tribunal business, it is in the interest of justice for Judge Argibay and I to continue sitting in absence of Judge Liu under Rule 15 bis. Any objection to these proceedings?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Please, Mr. McCloskey, the floor is yours. You may continue. I hope you finish today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I hope so, too. We'll try hard, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going to 65 ter number 235, a Bratunac Brigade military police log entry for 14/15 July 1995. We are going to need the registry to help with the documents. I hope the ELMO is working. We can put the English on the ELMO and provide the B/C/S to the witness. Mr. Nikolic, this says: "The police were engaged in the escort of Muslim refugees." What do you think that means?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of this document that I have in front of me, I see that the date is the 14th to the 15th of July, 1995. And it is a daily report. "The police was engaged in escorting Muslim refugees." So this refers to the participation of the police from the Bratunac Brigade military police platoon in escorting the convoy that went on the 14th towards Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. If we could go to the next exhibit, 65 ter 235 again, but the same Bratunac Brigade log sheet from the military police dated 15 July, 1995. It states: "The police worked on searching and combing the area as well as apprehending the Muslims found hiding in the area." Do you know anything about this statement, about the substance it's referring to?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really am not able to confirm what it says in this daily report, especially the sentence "the police worked on searching and combing the area as well as apprehending the Muslim found hiding in the area." So I'm unable to tell you exactly what this meant. I am not aware of this involvement of the police. I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We'll go to the next one. 65 ter 235, same Bratunac Brigade military police log dated 17 July, 1995. And referring you to the part where it says: "One police patrol remained in Pilica to guard the Muslims." Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew that a police patrol which was escorting the convoy stayed behind in Pilica. And I was informed about by the police commander, Mirko Jankovic, about this patrol that remained in Zvornik, or rather in the territory of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you testified about that previously today. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you can just remind us again, how many military police officers would have been in a patrol?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that a police patrol usually or as a rule consists of two to three policemen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, before we get to the next document, I want to ask you -- in fact, Madam Registrar, you might want to sit down for a minute. Can you tell us what a daily combat report is in a brigade.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A regular daily combat report is a report which is written every day, usually by the operations officer on duty.
